name: init
long:
git init creates an empty Git repository.
It sets up the .git directory with all metadata.

name: create branch
short: Create and switch to a new branch
long:
git checkout -b feature/login creates a new branch named "feature/login"
and switches your working copy to that branch.

name: make change
short: Create a new file on the feature branch
long:
This creates a file representing your feature work.
The change exists only on the current branch until merged.

name: git add
long: git add feature.txt stages the file so that the next commit includes it.

name: git commit
short: Commit changes to the feature branch
long:
git commit -m "Add feature file" records the staged changes
into the repository history on the current branch.

name: switch to main
long:
git checkout main switches your working copy back to the main branch,
preparing for a merge.

name: merge branch
long:
git merge feature/login integrates the feature branch's commits into main.
If there are conflicts, Git will prompt you to resolve them.

name: delete branch
short: Delete the merged feature branch locally
long:
git branch -d feature/login removes the local branch reference
after it has been merged.

name: git log
short: Show the commit history with a graph
long:
This is a readonly command; it does not change files.
git log --oneline --graph --decorate --all displays a compact
graph of commit history across branches.
